next_changelog: Added four precise, generalizable non-boundary rules to [Never Segment]: (1) don't split right after a causal/result connective (-다보니까/-아서/-니까) when the following clause's main verb hasn't appeared yet or shares an implicit subject with the preceding clause; (2) don't split inside a conditional chain (…하고 … -면) where the first clause has no complete predicate independent of the following if/when clause; (3) don't split where a discourse marker (또/그리고/근데) recurs on both sides of the boundary, which causes duplicated connectives in translation; (4) don't split right before a clause-final -고 that introduces a bare NP/predicate list still depending on the earlier clause's subject or copula.

Added four matching [Examples — Do NOT Segment] entries (generalized, not copied from evaluation data) illustrating each new rule, bringing the section to the 12-example cap without removing existing entries since the limit was not previously reached.

next_changelog: [When to Segment]: Added three concrete permissive rules to increase splitting frequency: (1) internal sentence-final punctuation ('.', '?') anywhere mid-utterance is always a mandatory split candidate, not only at the very end; (2) causal/additive connectives (그래서/그러니까/그런데/근데) mark a valid split point as soon as the preceding clause has a complete predicate, even if what follows is short or trails off — a short/incomplete remainder is never a reason to withhold the split; (3) coordinate -고/-며 clauses with independently resolved subjects/objects on each side are a valid split point without waiting for later material.

[Never Segment]: Narrowed the causal/result connective prohibition so it only blocks a split when clause B has NOT YET reached any predicate at all (a bare fragment) — removed the broader 'shares implicit subject' clause that was causing over-cautious under-segmentation; once B reaches its own complete predicate, splitting is allowed even with a shared subject. Also added a clarifying sentence restricting the conditional-chain prohibition strictly to the '…하고 … -면/-거든' pattern so it no longer discourages ordinary -고 coordination between two already-complete predicates, which is now explicitly permitted under [When to Segment].

next_changelog: [When to Segment]: Added explicit permissive rules to fix under-segmentation: (1) 그런데/근데/그래서/그러니까 always mark a valid split the instant the prior clause has a complete predicate, even if what follows is itself another connective-headed clause — segment at the FIRST such boundary, don't wait for a later one; (2) any -고/-며 coordination between two clauses that each have their own subject and verb (subject may be pro-dropped but recoverable from the immediately preceding NP) is always a valid split point, without waiting for confirmation from later material; (3) clarified that '?' or '.' occurring on a bare word/short phrase mid-utterance (not just after a full sentence) is still a mandatory split candidate.

[Never Segment]: Narrowed two over-broad prohibitions that were causing missed splits: the 'duplicated discourse marker' rule now only blocks a boundary when the identical marker token repeats with NO intervening complete clause between the two occurrences (not just general co-occurrence); the 'dependent NP list' rule now only blocks bare noun-phrase lists with no verb at all, and explicitly no longer applies once the following material contains its own complete predicate — such cases must be split per the new coordinate-clause rule in [When to Segment].

next_changelog: [Core Principles]: Strengthened the final 'when in doubt, split' bullet into an explicit left-to-right scanning rule: once a connective-ending or punctuation boundary is reached and it already closes a complete predicate, take that split immediately rather than waiting for a later, 'safer-looking' boundary further on. This directly targets under-segmentation (long multi-clause sentences left whole despite clear early connective/punctuation boundaries) without adding any new prohibition — it only clarifies the existing bias-to-split principle.

No examples were removed since the section remains under the 12-example cap (11/12).

next_changelog: [When to Segment]: Added a new bullet clarifying that connective-based (그런데/근데/그래서/그러니까) and coordinate -고/-며 split points must be taken independently each time they occur, regardless of sentence length or how many other clauses remain unresolved in the same long utterance — a long sentence with only one qualifying boundary should still be split there rather than left whole, and a sentence with several qualifying boundaries should be split at every one of them, not just the first.

[Never Segment]: Narrowed the 'mid-clause, before the verb/predicate has appeared' prohibition by adding an explicit exemption: this prohibition does not apply when the candidate boundary coincides with an existing terminal punctuation mark ('.', '?', '!') in the transcript, since such punctuation already marks a speaker/transcriber-intended completed unit and overrides the predicate-completeness check.
